clue.text: Hold up, crossworders, the first of these is tough

parts.note: a hold-up at the bank is a robbery, so to hold up is to rob
the setter is addressing the people solving this, and we crossworders are US

indicators.note: picking out the first of a group means keeping only what stands at its head, so a single opening letter survives

parts.note: the head of the word 'these' is T

explanation.walkthrough: The comma is the disguise: 'Hold up, crossworders' reads as the setter asking us to wait a moment, and is really an instruction plus a word for the people addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: tough -> ROBUST: robust describes something built to take punishment, the sturdy sense of tough rather than the harsh or chewy one.

clue.text: Savage without one book?

parts.note: Ruth is one of the books of the Old Testament, and the question mark owns up to naming a single example
coffee without sugar is sugarless, so without does the same job as less

explanation.walkthrough: Read as English the clue pictures a brute with nothing to read; read as wordplay, 'without' stops being a preposition and becomes a word in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage -> RUTHLESS: both are adjectives for cruelty done without pity, describing someone who feels no compunction about the damage.

clue.text: Arranged rags in one music genre, and another

indicators.note: to arrange things is to put them in an order of your own choosing, and the order chosen is not the one printed
whatever is set in something else ends up embedded inside it, so these letters land within the word named next

parts.note: the blues is a music genre, and the word opens up after its fourth letter
the four letters of rags, reordered, drop into that gap

explanation.walkthrough: Rags earns its place on the surface because ragtime sits beside the blues as a genre, which is exactly why it does not look like fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: another -> BLUEGRASS: the wordplay names the blues, and the definition asks for a second genre, the banjo-driven Appalachian string-band music.

clue.text: Key change

definitions.meaning: the key on every keyboard held down to type capitals or alternate symbols
a change in the weather or in opinion, often gradual rather than sudden

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions with nothing between them, and the join is hidden because 'key change' is a phrase in its own right, the musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Key -> SHIFT names one particular keyboard key; change -> SHIFT is the ordinary noun for a movement from one state to another.

clue.text: Loaded footballers turned voluble

indicators.note: a thing turned round is facing the other way, so those two letters are read in the opposite order

parts.note: the FA is the association that runs the English game and stands in for its players; turned round it reads AF
someone voluble talks readily and easily, which is what fluent means

explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' is the misdirection. Beside talkative footballers it wants to mean drunk, and the sense the answer needs is rich.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded -> AFFLUENT: loaded is the slang way of saying somebody has plenty of money, which is the wealth affluent describes.

clue.text: Puck perhaps tacked on to make characters behave improperly

indicators.note: anything tacked on is fastened to the end of what was already there, so that piece brings up the rear

parts.note: to forge a horseshoe or an alliance is to make it
the tone of a place is its character, and both words take a plural the same way
Puck is the elf of A Midsummer Night's Dream, and 'perhaps' admits he is only one example

explanation.walkthrough: The sentence points the wrong way: 'make characters behave' reads as a stage direction, and only 'tacked on to' gives away that Puck is a chunk of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: behave improperly -> FORGET ONESELF: to forget oneself is to let your manners slip and do what the occasion did not allow.

clue.text: Low on energy, pureed the garlic

indicators.note: food that has been pureed is reduced to a smooth mass, with nothing left where it started

parts.note: the nine letters of THE GARLIC, stirred into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a cook explaining why the garlic got pureed rather than chopped, which hides the fact that those two words are the raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: Low on energy -> LETHARGIC: the adjective for a body running short of vigour, sluggish and slow to stir itself.

clue.text: Go in, letting person cut in front

indicators.note: a cut made at the front takes the head off, so the word loses the letter that was leading it

parts.note: a renter is the person who lets a property out, and its leading R is about to go

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut in front' does two jobs at once: the queue-jumping the surface describes, and the instruction to lop a letter off the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Go in -> ENTER: enter is the plain verb for crossing a threshold, and it matches the imperative the clue is written in.

clue.text: Singer starts to truly hate prog band

indicators.note: the start of a word is where it begins, so only the opening letter of each word named is taken

parts.note: the initial letters of those two words are T and H
Rush are the Canadian trio, one of prog rock's best-known bands

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a music snob's verdict, which is what keeps you from noticing that 'prog band' wants an actual group's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Singer -> THRUSH: a thrush is a songbird, so the clue names the bird by the thing it is famous for doing.

clue.text: Travel business to ancient city is minute

parts.note: the preposition is taken at face value, letter for letter
Ur in Mesopotamia is the crossword's standing ancient city
the verb is lifted straight out of the clue as two letters
m is the standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.walkthrough: Only the city is a synonym here. Everything else is built from the small grammatical words the clue is written with, which is why they read as joinery.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel business -> TOURISM: tourism is the industry that sells travel, hotels and sightseeing, so the phrase names the trade rather than the traveller.

clue.text: In which data plotter probes gathered material like steel?

definitions.text: In which data plotter probes gathered material like steel?

parts.note: a crowd that gathered met, so gathered gives MET

indicators.note: a probe goes into whatever it is examining, so those letters push inside the word beside them

parts.note: steel is an alloy of iron and carbon, and the word splits before its final letter
a graph is what plots data against a pair of axes

explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one: read it as a sentence and it describes a laboratory, read it as instructions and every word is also doing a job on letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: metallography is the laboratory study in which gathered metal samples are examined and their structure recorded.

clue.text: Rubbish art mixed up with old Turner

indicators.note: letters mixed up together lose the arrangement they arrived in and have to be sorted into a new one

parts.note: rot is what you call something rubbish - he talks utter rot
the word goes into the mix exactly as it is printed
o is the standard abbreviation for old, as in OAP

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Turner' is a painter on the surface and the clue would love you to hunt for JMW; the word it wants is the everyday one for anything that goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Turner -> ROTATOR: a rotator is any part or machine that turns something, so the -er agent noun matches the -or one in job and number.

clue.text: Weak understanding

definitions.meaning: weak in intensity, as in a mild drizzle or a lenient sentence
the flash of comprehension when something finally makes sense, or what a good explanation sheds on a problem

explanation.walkthrough: Two words, two definitions and no wordplay at all - the pair reads as one phrase about a feeble grasp of something, and that is the whole disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak -> LIGHT is the sense of a light touch or a light punishment; understanding -> LIGHT is the illumination somebody sheds on a problem.

clue.text: So keeps bloke from Genesis at front of record book

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold on to it, so the outer word closes around whatever it is holding

parts.note: so and thus are interchangeable - 'so it follows', 'thus it follows' - and the word parts in the middle
Esau, Jacob's hairy elder brother, is a man out of the book of Genesis

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, and that single letter is all that is wanted

parts.note: the front letter of 'record'

explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'So' a Peter Gabriel album and the bloke from Genesis his old band; the setter means the plain word and the Bible's first book.
explanation.definitionFit: book -> THESAURUS: a thesaurus is a reference volume of synonyms, so the definition names it by the wider class it belongs to.

clue.text: Scrutinise modern gal spreading gossip

indicators.note: whatever is spread gets scattered over a wider area and no longer sits in the arrangement it started in

parts.note: to scan a document is to scrutinise it
the nine letters of MODERN GAL, scattered into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spreading gossip' is the phrase the surface wants read whole, and prising the two words apart is the solve: one is an instruction, the other the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: gossip -> SCANDALMONGER: gossip names a person as well as the talk, and a scandalmonger is that person, one who trades in other people's disgrace.

clue.text: Cleared up stretch with races on?

definitions.text: Cleared up stretch with races on?

indicators.note: read upwards, which in a down entry means from the foot of the answer towards its head, so those letters arrive the other way round
one thing resting on another sits above it, and in a down entry above means earlier in the answer

parts.note: to be cleared of a debt is to be rid of it, and RID climbing the grid reads DIR
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy, the most famous motorcycle races there are
a rack is the frame that stretches whatever is tied to it

explanation.walkthrough: An all-in-one, and an unusually literal one: the racing in the surface really is racing, so nothing here has to be re-read except 'cleared' and 'stretch'.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a dirt track is a cleared strip of bare earth with speedway or motorcycle racing run on it.

clue.text: Regularly see defeat?

parts.note: a rout is a defeat so complete that the losers run
a bishop's see is his cathedral city and Ely is the stock one; a defeat there is a defeat IN ELY, which supplies the little word as well

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is doing the work. 'See defeat' is not a synonym but a place to put one, and the answer splits into exactly that small scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Regularly -> ROUTINELY: something done routinely happens as a matter of routine, at regular intervals rather than by chance.

clue.text: Catching show's opening, pan range of talent

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it and keep it in your grasp, so the word closes over whatever it catches

parts.note: a skillet is a frying pan, and it takes the newcomer in after its fifth letter

indicators.note: the opening of a word is the letter it begins with, and only that one is used

parts.note: the opening letter of 'show's'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' as a verb - to review something harshly - is what the surface offers, and the noun is what the wordplay needs: a heavy iron frying pan.
explanation.definitionFit: range of talent -> SKILL SET: a skill set is the collection of things a person can do, so the phrase names the spread of abilities they bring.

clue.text: Disney toon to inspire about half of crooner's rock album

indicators.note: letters written about something are wrapped round it, so this word opens and everything else goes inside

parts.note: to inspire is to breathe in, and to suck is to draw in the same way; the word parts after its first letter

indicators.note: you keep only as far as the midpoint of the word, and it is the front half that survives

parts.note: the first four of the eight letters of CROONER'S
a rock is a jewel - the enormous rock on her finger
the album you buy in a shop is a CD

explanation.walkthrough: Inspire means breathe in long before it means encourage, and it is that older sense which hands over the word that swallows everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Disney toon -> SCROOGE MCDUCK: the miserly duck is a Disney cartoon character, so the definition names him by the studio that draws him.

clue.text: Cool doctor under retro dad look

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards to an earlier style, and these two letters are read backwards too
in a down clue whatever is under something sits lower in the grid, so those letters come last

parts.note: dad is PA, and PA turned round is AP
lo is the old word for look - lo and behold
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the degree a doctor holds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro dad' sounds like a man in a vintage shirt, and is really the reversal instruction sitting next to the two letters it acts on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cool -> APLOMB: aplomb is composure kept under pressure, the poised sense of cool rather than the temperature or the fashionable one.

clue.text: Case favoured Pennsylvania city beyond its state

indicators.note: whatever lies beyond something has been passed and left behind it, so those letters follow the ones they are beyond

parts.note: Pennsylvania's postal abbreviation is PA
a pet theory or a pet subject is a favoured one
Erie stands on the lake of the same name in the north-west corner of the state

explanation.walkthrough: Pennsylvania is clued twice over. It is named once for the city that sits in it, then pointed at again as 'its state', where only the two-letter form fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Case -> PAPETERIE: a papeterie is a writing case, the fitted box holding paper, envelopes and pens, so 'case' names it by its wider kind.

clue.text: Pasty and doughnut diet for Americans?

parts.note: a pasty complexion is a pale one
a ring doughnut is a circle with a hole in it, which draws an O

explanation.walkthrough: Both wordplay words are things you eat, which is what holds the surface still; only 'pasty' has to be re-read, as an adjective rather than a Cornish supper.
explanation.definitionFit: diet for Americans? -> PALEO: the caveman-style eating plan, spelt the American way, since British English would write palaeo with the extra a.

clue.text: Material desire follows lust in the end

indicators.note: what follows something comes along behind it, so this piece is placed second
the end of a word is where its final letter sits, and that letter is all the clue takes

parts.note: the last letter of 'lust'
will is desire as a noun - doing something against your will

explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire follows lust' reads as a single idea about appetite and is really two separate instructions, which is how the answer's one-letter opening stays hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Material -> TWILL: twill is a cloth woven in diagonal ridges, denim being the everyday example, so the definition names it by its kind.

clue.text: Absolute child verges on animal

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: a verge is the edge of a road, so it is the edges of the word that are taken and the middle that is left out

parts.note: the two edges of ANIMAL are A and L

explanation.walkthrough: 'Verges on animal' looks like a judgement about somebody's behaviour and is a pair of tweezers picking off the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute -> TOTAL: a total ban and an absolute ban are the same thing, the sense of complete with nothing at all held back.

clue.text: Light reflected through strip mall I operate

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing the wrong way round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
something running through a phrase passes across the words in it, ignoring where they break

parts.note: the run striP MALL I Operate carries PMALLIO, which read backwards is the answer

explanation.walkthrough: A shopping-centre surface with the answer lying across four words of it, and 'reflected' is the only thing telling you which way to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Light -> OIL LAMP: the answer is one particular kind of light, a wick burning in a reservoir of oil, so the definition names the class.

clue.text: Fine to watch stripping with good health

parts.note: F is the pencil grade for fine, and the standard crossword abbreviation

indicators.note: to strip something is to take a layer off it, and what comes off here is the letter named right beside it

parts.note: to witness an event is to watch it happen
w is the everyday abbreviation for with, and it is the letter stripped off the front

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stripping with' reads as one phrase about undressing. Split it and 'with' stops being a preposition, becoming the letter that has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: good health -> FITNESS: fitness is bodily condition at its best, the state of being fit, so it names health as a measurable quality.

clue.text: Bear left at backwards New York borough

indicators.note: an across answer read backwards runs right to left, so those two letters arrive in the reverse of their usual order

parts.note: to brook no argument is to bear none, so brook is bear in the sense of tolerate
L is the map and stage abbreviation for left
New York shortens to NY, which is turned round to read YN

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear left at' is a driving instruction on the surface and three separate scraps of wordplay underneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: borough -> BROOKLYN: New York City is divided into five boroughs and Brooklyn is one of them, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Casually try produce coated in bit of butter

indicators.note: a coating goes all the way round whatever it covers, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a pat of butter is the small slab served beside the bread
a hen produces eggs by laying them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of butter' looks like an instruction to take a piece of a word and is not one: the whole phrase yields a single three-letter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Casually try -> PLAY AT: to play at something is to dabble in it without commitment, the half-hearted attempt the definition describes.
